page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number top left. One column of verse, full width, in stanzas. Catchword alone at the lower right, below the last line.

p.i: Tyrrhenis, Siculis, cum Balearibus, Et Sardis miseris, Illipulensibus, Vicinisque Abyla Gadibus ultimis, Nec non Calaicis, Cantabricis quoque, Nereu, parce: Dolor nam satis occupat Matrum corda suos usque gementium, Qui luctum reliqua spargit Jberia.
Sic olim Pharios contumulat vorax Rubra gurges aquae (nam Tomyrin Scytis Linquo, Persa cui succubuit cadens)
Apparet tamen heic dextera fortior, (Fas hoc dicere sit, Numine non graui, Cuius dextra duplex, hoc opus edidit.) Quàm cum sunt Pharii pondere plumbeo Damnati tumidis vorticibus semel.
Nam tunc una fuit gens grauis Isaco. Jurata exitio multa fuit tuo.
Non assueta Pharos Martia tangere Instrumenta, fluit mollis odoribus: Ast hi Martigenae sunt populi simul Marti convitium qui facerent patri.
Vecti sunt Pharii curriculis Salo Non aptis, medys currere nec vadis: Hi celsis trabibus perfreta caerula Tranant remigijs aequora turgida.
Moses Isacidis praefuit: (acrior Quo non vllus erat, vel sapientior) Heic, quis crediderit? foemina dux fuit.

page.notes: Catchword "Angusto" is in a larger italic hand at the lower right and is taken as the printed catchword. Lines were joined within each stanza; stanza breaks follow the printed indents. "Iberia" and "Iurata" were given consonant J per rule 5. Possible printing errors left as printed: "medys" (line 4 of stanza 5), "Tomyrin", "Tranant". Words of the first stanza with ambiguous letters were read as printed. The word "Ast" is partly obscured by a stroke and may be read differently.
